text: The boss of a four and a half trillion dollar company just confessed a secret. The next day, his company lost almost two hundred billion dollars.
Jensen Huang started Nvidia in nineteen ninety-three, at a Denny's, with forty thousand dollars.
His chips were built for video games. Then they turned out to be perfect for AI.
Then, on November eighth, he emailed his staff: I was unfaithful to my wife.
Reports say U.S. intelligence suspects the woman of spying for China. China calls that groundless.
The board opened an investigation, and says it has no reason to think secrets leaked. The stock still fell more than four percent.
Here's why that's your problem. Nvidia is about seven percent of the S and P five hundred. Own an index fund? Seven cents of every dollar rides on one company. And one man.
Investors call it key person risk.
So spread your money out. Companies are run by people. And people make mistakes.
